extracted.intended_audience: community program developers and nonprofit grant-seekers (state/local organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, step-by-step guide for planning, researching, writing, budgeting, and submitting grant proposals for community programs and nonprofit organizations seeking project funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs assessment / Problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The needs assessment or problem statement forms the basis for the development of the project and the request for project funding. A proposal is a written expression of, and proposed solution to, a problem; it must present a persuasive argument for the organization's case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect background facts and data to support claims; use local data when possible; combine raw data and public opinion; do your homework but don't inundate reviewers with statistics. Differentiate national statistics from local data and document real (not imagined) service gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background information funders expect
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders expect clear answers about the applicant organization's identity, history, qualifications, board role, and board approval/commitment for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to describe: who the organization is and its history; qualifications to perform the program; the board's role in policy and in project development; whether the board approved and is committed to implementation. Funders may contact board members to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and objectives clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what need is being met, define the problem clearly, describe the proposed program, state specific objectives, list activities to achieve objectives, provide a realistic timetable, and define the target population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify target population size and geographic boundaries, whether the target population had input, how they will benefit, and how the project differs from similar programs (uniqueness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and management plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the organization will implement and manage the program, where it fits in current structure, staffing (existing or needed), and qualifications of key staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain management and reporting lines, staff adequacy or hiring plans, and how the project fits within organizational capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the means to ensure stated needs and objectives are met, provisions for evaluation, and whether project results will be shared with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evaluation methods, who will conduct evaluation, indicators/outcomes, reporting plans, and plans to disseminate findings to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget completeness and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide total project cost, amount requested, and clear line-item budget with explanation of costs and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include typical line item costs, justify each item, show whether in-kind or cash match will be provided, and show requests to other funders and status of those requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of future funding / sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Address how the project will continue after the initial grant ends and what other funding sources might sustain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss alternative funding, plans for continuation, timing for seeking follow-on support, and whether the project is designed to be time-limited or sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use empirical methods to determine community needs, such as personal observation, aggregation of reports (intake forms, hotlines), and community surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods appropriate to organization capacity (door-to-door canvass, public forums, intake log tabulation); surveys offer direct client input and may require technical assistance; personal observation is inexpensive but limited in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of credible statistical and documentary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with appropriate statistical data and documentary evidence from sources like the Census Bureau, state agencies, universities, RPCs, and health/public aid reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local data where possible; cite publications (e.g., Census reports, state health reports); use computerized resources (CENDATA, FastFax, state data centers) and university/regional planning resources for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze empirical and secondary data to identify types and severity of needs, who exhibits needs, and where they are located; compare segments over time or between areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce interpretable comparisons (which segments most affected, trends, rates of service change, resource allocations); develop a checklist or socioeconomic report summarizing clients, households, income, housing, services in use, attitudes, and pockets needing attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for needs-analysis content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure needs analysis includes description of potential clients (age, sex, race), families/households, income analysis, community habitats, significant segments, services in use and attitudes, important relationships, areas needing improvement, and groups needing special attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider producing a socioeconomic report with numerical breakdowns and graphics linking demographics to services (e.g., hospital beds, employment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy development (idea generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a set of strategies to address identified problems through brainstorming, researching government projects, and researching private initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brainstorming with staff/board/experts; examine federal/state programs (JTPA, CSBG, CDBG, etc.) for fit; adapt strategies from privately funded projects and evaluation reports when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of strategies (vetting questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze each proposed strategy for merit considering organizational capacity, available resources, constraints and ways to neutralize blockers, client participation, unintended effects, cost-effectiveness, prior successes elsewhere, consistency with organizational philosophy, staff acceptance, and duplication of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided list of diagnostic questions (Can we carry it out? Who might prevent us? Would clients participate? Is it cheapest/easiest? Has it been tried elsewhere? etc.) when selecting the final approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting proper funding agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Target funding agencies with compatible interests and ensure special forms or certifications are identified in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funder priorities and application formats; avoid submitting to agencies that don't match your program goals; determine required certifications and paperwork before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of proposal submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine and meet deadlines; understand that many grants are awarded once a year and late or incomplete submissions may be rejected immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission calendar, allow time for reviews and signatures, and confirm funding cycles and deadlines with the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts and decision makers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and cultivate contacts and decision makers at the funding agency and track communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify program officers, agency directors, and local/regional contacts; establish relationships and record contact attempts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track contacts and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of all outreach to funders and local partners, including who you spoke to, when, and what was decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contact logs to follow up appropriately and to provide evidence of due diligence and outreach when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining local support and stakeholder buy-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain written support and clearances from board members, project collaborators, clients, support agencies, and federal regional agencies (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate discussions with affected groups, run publicity campaigns, ensure support letters are genuine and substantive, and clear the project with all interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support letters should be true letters of support: addressed to the agency director or board chairman and should reflect knowledge of the organization and familiarity with the proposed project and pledge of assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or obviously solicited letters; letters should show specific endorsement and knowledge of the organization's track record and the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibilities of renewal / continuation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and describe how the program will be sustained beyond the initial grant period (usually 1–3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify potential future funders, partnerships, or revenue streams that could continue the project; explain transition plans if grant-funded positions or activities are temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get expert advice / use technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize professionals (internal staff or outside consultants), fundraising consultants, other program sponsors, state technical assistance staff, local professionals, and educational institutions to refine ideas and increase credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider hiring or consulting with experts for needs assessments, evaluation design, budgeting, or proposal review; attend Foundation Center or Donors Forum seminars and use cooperating collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding common grantseeking errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and avoid routine errors such as missing required forms/certifications, poor timing, lack of local support, vague budgets, and insufficient documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm application requirements in advance, meet deadlines, ensure completeness, and include all requested documentation to avoid immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal writing tips (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow basic organization and clarity principles when writing: be clear about mission, engage in systematic planning, develop realistic strategies, and stay within organizational mission scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate funder questions into the proposal body when funders lack standard forms; be concise, organized, persuasive, and realistic about capacity and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a cover letter that introduces the proposal and summarizes the project's purpose and funding request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it concise, addressed properly, and tailored to the funder; highlight unique points and request amount; provide contact information for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal summary / executive summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary that encapsulates the problem, proposed solution, objectives, target population, budget request, timetable, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the summary standalone and persuasive—reviewers often read it first; be concise and include key facts and the request amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction / organizational description
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce the organization, mission, history, capabilities, and relationship to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate organizational capacity, relevant past performance, and how the project fits into the organization's overall activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (specific, measurable)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives and the activities that will be carried out to achieve them; objectives should be realistic and tied to evaluation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurable outcomes, timeline, and link activities to objectives; ensure objectives align with identified needs and funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / program design
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the activities, curriculum or services, staffing, timeline, and operational plan that will accomplish objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sufficient detail for reviewers to judge feasibility: who will do what, timeline, materials, recruitment and participation strategies, and link to staffing and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan (methods & indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how success will be measured, what data will be collected, who will evaluate, and how findings will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include performance indicators, data collection instruments, frequency of measurement, responsible parties, and dissemination plans; share results with others as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical line item costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must include typical line items (personnel, fringe, travel, equipment, supplies, contracts, indirect costs) and realistic cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain each line item, include basis for cost estimates, apply funder limits on categories, and ensure consistency between budget and narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching share / in-kind contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify any required matching share and describe in-kind or cash contributions the organization will provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document valuation of in-kind contributions, timing of matches, and source of matching funds; ensure match meets funder rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow and timing of expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Address cash flow needs and the timing of when funds will be spent, including how the organization will bridge gaps if reimbursements are delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show projected cash flow by period, note any front-loaded costs, and describe mechanisms (reserves, bridges) to maintain operations until funds are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix content (supporting materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include typical appendix items that support the proposal such as resumes, letters of support, organizational charts, financial statements, and relevant publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include necessary, clearly labeled documents; avoid overloading appendix with irrelevant material; include items requested by funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic and library resources for funder research
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ databases and electronic resources (Foundation Center, GRANTS database, DIALOG, FAPRS, ILLINET, Access Illinois) to locate appropriate funders and past awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online databases to identify funders by subject/geography, study past grant awards, and learn funder priorities and application patterns.
